summary: Current air quality in Delhi is Very Poor (AQI 301). Household has high-risk age groups (children/elderly), and 1 sensitive health condition(s). Prioritize protective indoor safeguards and low-emission choices.

routine.action: Wear a well-fitted N95 or FFP2 respirator outdoors
routine.why: AQI is 301 (Very Poor). Standard cloth or surgical masks do not filter fine PM2.5 aerosols.
routine.impact: Roughly 95% fine particle filtration efficiency when fitted with a tight perimeter seal (NIOSH/CPCB test basis).

routine.action: Shift all aerobic exercise and active play strictly indoors
routine.why: Deep breathing during outdoor exertion increases particulate deposition in sensitive lungs by 3 to 5 times, especially risky for children and seniors.
routine.impact: Roughly 60% to 80% reduction in total inhaled aerosol volume compared to exercising outdoors (aerosol medicine study basis).

routine.action: Prepare emergency medical kit, rescue inhalers, and symptom checklist
routine.why: Identified elevated risk (heart). Smog triggers rapid bronchial spasms and cardiovascular stress.
routine.impact: About 50% reduction in severe asthma attack escalation when rescue medication is initiated at earliest symptom onset (clinical asthma guidelines basis).

routine.action: Adjust commute departure away from peak morning inversion (avoid 7:00 AM - 9:30 AM)
routine.why: Surface-level pollutant concentrations peak during morning rush hour combined with cold winter boundary layer compression.
routine.impact: About 20% to 35% lower commuter exposure to direct tailpipe carbon monoxide and black carbon (urban transit exposure basis).

indoor.action: Run a mid-capacity True HEPA air purifier continuously in the primary bedroom
indoor.why: True HEPA captures sub-micron combustion particles without producing secondary ozone. Sleeping in clean air aids lung recovery.
indoor.impact: Roughly 75% to 85% reduction in bedroom PM2.5 concentrations in a closed room (standard CADR test basis).

indoor.action: Keep windows and balcony doors sealed; place rolled damp towels along drafty door thresholds
indoor.why: Hazardous outdoor air rapidly infiltrates homes through window cracks and doorway gaps during stagnant winter inversions.
indoor.impact: Roughly 40% to 60% reduction in outdoor-to-indoor particulate infiltration rate (building envelope research basis).

indoor.action: Strictly avoid incense (agarbatti), mosquito coils, and scented candles indoors
indoor.why: Burning one mosquito coil or incense stick generates fine particulate concentrations equivalent to several tens of cigarettes in an unventilated room.
indoor.impact: Avoids adding roughly 100 to 250 µg/m³ of internal PM2.5 load into living spaces (combustion emissions study basis).

swaps.action: Operate kitchen exhaust fan continuously and cook with tight-fitting lids on burners
swaps.why: Gas combustion releases nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and ultrafine particles that exacerbate bronchial hyper-reactivity.
swaps.impact: About 35% to 55% reduction in indoor peak NO2 and aerosol peaks during active boiling/frying (kitchen ventilation study basis).

swaps.action: Shift to metro rail transit or set vehicle AC to 100% recirculation mode with a cabin PM2.5 filter
swaps.why: Metro transit removes you from surface exhaust corridors; cabin recirculation blocks highway particulate ingress.
swaps.impact: Roughly 70% reduction in in-cabin particle exposure and about 2 kg CO2 avoided per transit trip (transportation research basis).

swaps.action: Compost or bag organic garden/kitchen waste; strictly avoid burning dry leaves or trash
swaps.why: Open biomass burning produces dense polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and toxic smoke at ground level during stagnant winter nights.
swaps.impact: Avoids releasing roughly 15 to 30 grams of pure fine particulate matter per small pile burned (CPCB emission inventory basis).
